known_limitations: PoC is a self-contained workload around exact Git-blob JSProxy bytes and modeled async CloseResultSet versus sync getEntry; it is not a full OpenHarmony build or a live distributed KV store run.

ThreadSanitizer proves unsynchronized shared_ptr owner accesses in the modeled call patterns; it does not prove a stable crash, memory corruption, data disclosure, privilege escalation, or exploitable stability.
The source-visible ArkTS/JS entry is partial; runtime permission enforcement, product module resolution, deployed image/version scope and cross-app/remote attacker control remain unknown.
fixed_control_mutex is an independently authored safe control; patched_atomic_minimal is a proposed local patch, not an upstream fix.
CWE-416 is only a possible consequence and remains unproven without product-level use-after-free evidence.
Git blob payload SHA-256 is canonical; checkout SHA-256 is separately recorded because repository line-ending filters change working-tree bytes.
source_hash_semantics: sha256 is the canonical Git blob payload hash; checkout_sha256 is the raw local working-tree byte hash
product_build_blockers: component checkout lacks the OpenHarmony //build tree and complete external dependency closure

minimum_evidence_requirements: Built product component or device image identity plus exact build manifest, dependency/toolchain versions and reproducible build command.
Runtime policy trace for getResultSet/getEntry/closeResultSet including permission checks, app identity, sandbox/user boundary and exported IPC surface.
Instrumented product run showing thread IDs, NAPI execute/complete queues and the exact CloseResultSet/getEntry overlap window.
Crash or sanitizer trace in the product process plus memory/ABI diagnosis sufficient to distinguish shared_ptr owner UB from result-set use-after-close.
Independent CIA evidence: availability failure rate, integrity effect on returned entries, and confidentiality boundary including same-app versus cross-app/device data.
Attacker control model: who can call or induce the sequence, required privilege, input constraints, rate/window control and deployment reachability.
Patch applied to the real component and vulnerable/fixed/patched repeated runs under identical product build/profile.
